A hobbyist approach usually starts with a simple pin tumbler lock. The process involves inserting a tension wrench into the keyway to apply a slight rotational force to the lock’s plug. This tension is critical because it keeps the pins from falling back into place. Simultaneously, a pick—often a thin, hooked tool—is used to lift each pin individually. As each pin is raised to the "shear line" (the point where the pins align), the lock’s internal mechanism begins to shift. Once all the pins are aligned, the plug can be turned, and the lock opens.
